source.title: Scaling Laws and Pathologies of Single-Layer PINNs: Network Width and PDE Nonlinearity

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices and tables, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Extends empirical scaling-law analysis to single-layer physics-informed neural networks on PDE solution errors, a different domain from language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The study does not measure language-model cross-entropy, token or compute scaling, extrapolation to larger language models, or compute-optimal allocation. Its directly relevant results are the PINN width/nonlinearity scaling fits and their dependence on activation, PDE, and fit form.
record.test_reason: The study tests width–error scaling in a new training regime, single-layer physics-informed neural networks, bearing on V5 and setup-dependent scaling under V7. It does not test language-model pretraining laws.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors attribute generally flat or adverse width scaling to optimization limitations and identify PDE-dependent, nonseparable behavior for ReLU. They report no significant tanh interaction, consistent with the correctly read Table 3. Their blanket description of near-zero or negative width exponents overlooks the positive tanh Sine-Gordon result at κ = 8. Optimization and spectral bias are their interpretation; these experiments do not isolate them causally.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies PINN solution error on PDEs rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy; it sweeps width and a PDE hardness parameter, not parameter count, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with PDE, activation (ReLU versus tanh), and hardness κ. The authors also compare separable and width–hardness interaction fits; for ReLU the interaction is significant in the nonlinear PDEs, while the prose reports no significant tanh interaction, although the KdV tanh table entry carries **.
record.peer_reviewed: Machine Learning and the Physical Sciences Workshop (NeurIPS 2025)
record.problems: The tested setting is restricted to single-layer networks, Adam, one spatial dimension, and a small set of PDEs; the results do not establish scaling behavior for language models. The paper reports five random seeds per configuration and confidence intervals, but the tanh Allen-Cahn separable fit has negative adjusted R². Appendix C's KdV tanh interaction entry is marked significant in the table, in tension with the prose stating that no tanh interaction term is significant.

untested.parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute over several orders of magnitude.
Prediction of larger runs from fits on smaller runs; no held-out scale extrapolation is evaluated.
Loss-minimising parameter and token allocation at fixed compute.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count; activation comparisons here do not establish that architecture matters little across a wide range.
Other modalities and regimes beyond these single-hidden-layer, one-dimensional PINNs; token/data and compute scaling, alternative optimizers, and convergence-controlled scaling.
Downstream performance versus pretraining loss or scale.
Parameter-counting conventions, schedule and fitting-procedure sensitivity, published language-model-law disagreements, and compute-optimal allocation.

record.verdict_notes: States for T1–T50 describe decreasing-error scaling under V5; their comparisons bear on V7. T51–T56 describe interaction evidence under V7. Negative exponents alone do not disprove a mathematical power-law form: the V5 challenges concern extending decreasing-error scaling to these settings. Runs use fixed 25,000-epoch Adam training over widths 16–1024, without demonstrating that optimization or data bottlenecks are removed. Nonseparability across width and hardness also does not rule out a power law at each fixed hardness.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out cross-entropy as a function of parameters, tokens, and compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Fixed-compute allocation between parameters and training tokens.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count, including depth versus width.
Tests scaling only for single-layer PINNs on the listed one-dimensional PDEs; does not test image/video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Downstream-task performance and its relationship to pretraining loss or scale.
Does not test language-model exponent choices, parameter counting, LM training schedules or data, published LM-law disagreements, or compute-optimal allocation.
